readme: Members of Broucke's families 7, 8 and 11 of the planar ER3BP, as polylines for the backdrops of the talk.

Each entry of 'families' is one member in one frame: family (7, 8 or 11), branch ('periapsis' for the members that start on the x axis at true anomaly theta0 = 0, 'apoapsis' for theta0 = pi), frame, begin ('ray' or 'golden', the point at which the record is begun, described below), thin (1 or 0, described below), the eccentricity e of the primaries, the mass ratio mu, theta0 in rad, bbox as [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax], t as the time of each point, theta as the true anomaly in rad of each point, and points as [x, y] over one period, from theta[0] to theta[0] + 2 pi, with the last point equal to the first.

The time t runs from 0 at the first point to 1 at the last, in proportion to the length along the polyline, except over the first and the last 0.1 of the time, in which the tip is sped up from rest and slowed to rest. Every strand is thus traced in the same time at an even pace.

The members are ordered by family, and within a family so that a staggered trace sweeps through it once, i.e. the periapsis branch from its largest e down to 0, then the apoapsis branch from 0 up. The member at e = 0 of the apoapsis branch is the orbit at e = 0 of the periapsis branch, begun on the other side of the x axis, hence it does not have a pulsating record.

A record with begin 'golden' is begun at a fraction of the length of its polyline, measured from the point at theta0, from the golden-ratio sequence over the members, with the same fraction in both frames, so that the starts of a drawing traced at once are spread evenly along it. The members with thin 1 take the first fractions of the sequence, and the others the next. A record with begin 'ray' is begun where the orbit crosses the ray from the secondary m2 at the polar angle 160 deg for family 7, 160 deg for family 8, and 175 deg for family 11, at the crossing farthest from m2, so that the members of a staggered trace are begun one after another at one place and are traced there in the same direction. Every member has an inertial record with begin 'golden', and two pulsating records, one with each begin. The two records of a member with begin 'golden' are begun at the same fraction of their lengths, hence at different samples. The records of a member hold the same samples, begun at different points, hence their lists theta hold the same values, rolled and shifted by 2 pi.

The key thin is 1 on every other member of the order above within a family, counted from the member at e = 0 of the periapsis branch, which has thin 1, and 0 on the other members. A drawing selected with thin=1 thus holds about half the members, spread evenly over the family. The member at e = 0 of the apoapsis branch is left out of this count and has thin 0.

Frame 'pulsating' is the rotating-pulsating frame (x, y), in which the primary m1 is fixed at (-mu, 0) and the secondary m2 at (1 - mu, 0). Frame 'inertial' is the barycentric inertial frame (xi, eta), i.e. the pulsating position scaled by the separation rho = (1 - e^2) / (1 + e cos theta) and rotated by theta about the barycenter, with the x axis of both frames on the line of apsides at theta = 0. Lengths are nondimensional, in units of the semi-major axis of the relative orbit of the primaries.
Each entry of 'bodies' gives the positions of m1 and m2 at theta = 0 in both frames, for one member.

About 12 members a branch are chosen evenly spaced in e. The samples of a member are kept jointly in both frames, at least one every 2 degrees of true anomaly, and more wherever the computed orbit is farther than 0.0003 from the chord, with coordinates rounded to 5 decimals.
